title: The Alternating Zeta Series and Analytic Continuation
problem: Starting from ζ(s) = Σ(n≥1) n^(-s) on Re(s) > 1, analyze η(s) = Σ(n≥1) (-1)^(n-1)n^(-s) as a complex series. Determine its convergence domain and prove the claim, not just pointwise convergence on the real axis. Where both series converge, derive their exact relationship. Then determine what can rigorously be concluded about continuing ζ(s) into 0 < Re(s) ≤ 1, including any exceptional points introduced by dividing by a factor that may vanish. Justify holomorphic claims with locally uniform convergence or an equivalent argument. State clearly what this method does not establish about the critical strip. No external sources or numerical computation are available; label recalled facts as such.

strategies.title: Abel summation and compact-uniform convergence
strategies.approach: Use bounded partial sums of the alternating signs with summation by parts. Establish convergence uniformly on each compact subset of the proposed half-plane, then use the theorem on locally uniform limits of holomorphic functions. Separately derive the relation with ζ only in its original absolute-convergence region and analyze whether algebraic division creates exceptional points.

strategies.title: Pairing terms and continuation boundary audit
strategies.approach: Group neighboring terms to expose cancellation and estimate the tail on compact subsets of the s-plane. Independently derive the relation to the original Dirichlet series by separating even and odd indices where rearrangement is licensed. Audit the pole and possible zeros of the multiplier before claiming continuation; identify what further argument would be needed beyond the half-plane reached by this series.
